title: Point-in-time recovery: restore Sunday's base backup, then replay the log up to just before a bad DELETE
captions: A full base backup runs every Sunday at 02:00. After it, the database keeps every write-ahead log (WAL) file in an archive. Together they hold every change since Sunday.
On Tuesday at 14:05, a script runs a DELETE without the right WHERE clause. The replica copies the DELETE a moment later. Replication cannot help you here.
You start a new, empty server and load Sunday's base backup into it. You do not touch the broken primary yet. It may still hold good writes you need.
You tell Postgres to replay the archived WAL and stop at 14:04:59. Every change up to that moment comes back. The DELETE, and everything after it, is skipped.
The rows are back. Good writes made after 14:05 are only on the old primary, so you copy them over by hand. The downtime runs until the app uses the new server. Compare both with your RPO and RTO.
